Senses.Explanation: Langye Huijue gives the servant-master reversal as his verdict on Zhaozhou probing Zhuyu's water and then walking away. The same record later puts the pair directly into Langye's answer after the source-unnamed questioner tries to cap his saying; Langye follows it with thirty blows. Dongchan Xiu uses it to answer why a supposedly benevolent spirit is struck by lightning. Across the turns, the saying names a reversal in which what should serve takes command and what should protect becomes exposed.

The World-Honored One is the Buddha as the Chan record repeatedly stages him: a public actor in cases who holds up a flower and entrusts it, mounts and leaves the teaching seat, pauses in an interview, points to or displays things, and is repeatedly re-raised and challenged by later masters. Those recurring acts define the invoked Zen figure here; the entry does not substitute an outside sacred biography. In the flower case, the World-Honored One holds up a flower before the assembly, Mahakasyapa smiles, and the World-Honored One entrusts him with the treasury of the true teaching eye, the wondrous mind of complete extinction, the subtle teaching gate beyond written words. In the teaching-seat case, the World-Honored One mounts the seat; Manjusri strikes the sounding block and tells the assembly to observe the teaching king's teaching; the World-Honored One then leaves the seat. When an outsider asks for neither speech nor no speech, the World-Honored One pauses for a while. He later tells Ananda that the outsider moved like a fine horse at the sight of the whip's shadow. The birth case is also repeatedly public: the World-Honored One points one hand upward and one downward, walks seven steps, looks in the four directions, and declares that he alone is honored. Yunmen Wenyan's separately attributed response is that he would have struck him dead, fed him to a dog, and thereby valued peace throughout the world. Other retained cases show the World-Honored One commanding Manjusri to bring a woman out of composure, naming Wangming Bodhisattva when Manjusri cannot, pointing to the ground for a temple before Indra plants one blade of grass, and displaying a color-changing jewel while questioning five heavenly kings. Later masters do not merely preserve a biography. Zhenjing Kewen recites the flower case, raises his staff, questions his own assembly, and strikes the incense table; Zhanran Yuancheng compares the World-Honored One's mounting and silence with the same visible acts by the people before him. Each named response or re-raising remains its own speaker's evidence and is not assigned to the World-Honored One.
